questions.stem: A recent Dun & Bradstreet study on 'zombie firms' in India draws on the concept of Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR). Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Interest Coverage Ratio (ICR) is calculated by dividing a company's profit before interest and taxes by its interest payable.
A firm with an ICR below 1 for three consecutive years is classified as a 'zombie firm'.
The Reserve Bank of India is the publisher of the zombie-firm classification referred to in the study.
A zombie firm typically continues to operate and service its debt through additional borrowing or capital raising, despite insufficient operating profit to cover interest costs.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct and match the standard definition of ICR and 'zombie firm' used in corporate stress analysis. Statement 3 is wrong because the study was conducted by Dun & Bradstreet, a private credit information company, not the RBI.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: The long shadow of 'zombie firms' on India Inc, in charts
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of corporate financial stress indicators (ICR, NPA-adjacent 'zombie firm' classification); similar to UPSC's recurring interest in banking/corporate stress metrics.

questions.stem: With reference to the right to privacy and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, which have come up in a Supreme Court challenge by media publishers, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 provides a blanket exemption for all journalistic activity from its data processing provisions.
The Supreme Court, in the K.S. Puttaswamy judgment, held that the right to privacy is intrinsic to the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct and is settled constitutional law since the 2017 Puttaswamy judgment. Statement 1 is incorrect — the petitioners' challenge is precisely that the Act fails to carve out any distinct exemption for journalistic processing, unlike laws such as the EU's GDPR.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Media association challenges privacy law in Supreme Court
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static concept of right to privacy as a fundamental right (Puttaswamy, 2017) and statutory exemptions in data protection law.

questions.stem: The Finance Minister recently reiterated India's fiscal consolidation roadmap. In this context, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The NK Singh Committee on FRBM review recommended a general government debt-to-GDP ceiling of 60%, to be shared equally as 30% for the Centre and 30% for the States.
The Union government has stated its aim to cap national debt at 50% of GDP by 2030.
The FRBM Act, 2003, in its original form, required the Union government to eliminate the revenue deficit by 31 March, 2009.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are correct — the FM's 50%-of-GDP-by-2030 target is the current stated goal, and the original FRBM Act, 2003 did target revenue deficit elimination by 2008-09. Statement 1 is wrong: the FRBM Review Committee (NK Singh, 2017) recommended an asymmetric split of 40% for the Centre and 20% for the States, not an equal 30:30 split.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Centre committed to reducing fiscal deficit, national debt to be capped at 50% of GDP by 2030: FM Sitharaman
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static FRBM Act/fiscal responsibility framework and the NK Singh Committee recommendations on debt-to-GDP targets.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of health/financial inclusion programmes and their nodal ministry or implementing agency:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Anaemia Mukt Bharat (7X7X7) Strategy
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Universal Salt Iodisation Programme
Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
National Family Health Survey
International Institute for Population Sciences
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
Ministry of Women and Child Development
questions.explanation: The first three pairs are correctly matched — Anaemia Mukt Bharat is run by the Health Ministry, salt iodisation standards fall under FSSAI, and NFHS is conducted by IIPS under MoHFW. The fourth pair is wrong: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana is implemented by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, not the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
questions.subject: Social Issues & Schemes
questions.sourceTitle: A ready solution to tackle anaemia
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional/nodal-ministry detail behind nutrition and financial inclusion schemes, a recurring 'scheme : ministry' pairs format.

questions.stem: The Finance Minister highlighted RTGS as part of India's payment infrastructure while inaugurating the RBI's new data centre. Which one of the following best describes the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system?
options: A system in which interbank fund transfers are settled individually and immediately on a one-to-one basis for high-value transactions, without netting of transactions.
A deferred net settlement system in which transactions are settled in batches at fixed intervals throughout the day.
A mobile-based instant payment interface enabling peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant transactions using a virtual payment address.
A 24x7 interbank electronic fund transfer system restricted to transactions below ₹2 lakh.
questions.explanation: RTGS settles each transaction individually and in real time without bundling or netting, making it suited for high-value transfers. Option B describes NEFT (batch/deferred net settlement), option C describes UPI, and option D misdescribes IMPS-type characteristics and inverts the value threshold — RTGS is actually used for high-value transfers above a minimum limit, not below ₹2 lakh.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: World's largest real-time payment system; 2,400 crore monthly transactions: FM Sitharaman on India's UPI revolution
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static distinction between RTGS, NEFT and UPI payment systems, a recurring Prelims theme on financial infrastructure.

questions.stem: In the context of rising Caesarean section rates highlighted by NFHS-6 data, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The World Health Organization has prescribed 10% as a mandatory Caesarean-section rate ceiling that every country must not exceed.
Statement-II: Population-level Caesarean section rates above 10% are not associated with reductions in maternal and newborn mortality, according to the WHO.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-II is correct and reflects the WHO's actual position that rates above 10% don't improve mortality outcomes. Statement-I is incorrect because the WHO explicitly does not recommend or mandate a specific target rate for any country, as the article clarifies.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Why West Bengal's C-Sections, at nearly 1 in 2 births, demand a hard look
questions.pyqLink: Tests precise knowledge of WHO public health guidance versus commonly misquoted 'target rates', relevant to health indicators under Science & Technology/Social Issues overlap.

questions.stem: Anthropic's IPO filing has drawn attention to artificial intelligence and public listing processes. Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: A Large Language Model (LLM) is a type of artificial intelligence system trained on vast amounts of text data to generate human-like language.
Generative Artificial Intelligence refers exclusively to AI systems that can process and generate text, and cannot generate images, audio, or video.
An Initial Public Offering (IPO) is the process by which a privately held company offers its shares to the public for the first time through a stock exchange.
In India, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the regulatory authority responsible for approving listings of Indian companies on foreign stock exchanges such as NASDAQ.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct standard definitions of LLMs and IPOs. Statement 2 is wrong because generative AI spans multiple modalities, not just text. Statement 4 is wrong because SEBI's jurisdiction covers Indian securities markets; listings on foreign exchanges like NASDAQ fall under that country's own regulator (e.g., the SEC in the US), not SEBI.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Anthropic points to AI dangers, soaring sales in IPO filing
questions.pyqLink: Tests static definitional knowledge of AI/LLM terminology and capital market regulatory jurisdiction, both recurring Science & Technology/Economy themes.

questions.stem: With reference to the appointment of the Chief Justice of a High Court in India, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President of India after consultation with the Collegium headed by the Chief Justice of India.
Statement-II: The Collegium system for recommending appointments and transfers of High Court Chief Justices is explicitly provided for under Article 217 of the Constitution of India.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: under Article 217, the President appoints High Court judges/Chief Justices after consultation with the CJI, Governor and outgoing Chief Justice, operationalised today through the Collegium's recommendation (as seen in the SC Collegium's recent proposals for Gujarat, Delhi, Telangana and Uttarakhand). Statement-II is incorrect because the Collegium system itself has no textual basis in the Constitution — it was evolved by the Supreme Court through the Second and Third Judges Cases interpreting 'consultation' in Articles 124 and 217 as 'concurrence'.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Supreme Court Collegium proposes four judges for HC Chief Justiceships
questions.pyqLink: Tests the constitutional vs judicially-evolved basis of the Collegium system, a recurring Polity PYQ theme (e.g., UPSC 2017 on NJAC and judicial appointments)

questions.stem: With reference to sugarcane pricing policy in India, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Fair and Remunerative Price (FRP) for sugarcane is fixed by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966.
State Governments are constitutionally barred from announcing any cane price higher than the FRP fixed by the Centre.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — FRP is a Centre-fixed statutory minimum price under the Sugarcane (Control) Order, 1966, based on CACP recommendations. Statement 2 is incorrect: several states, including Karnataka in the current Belagavi negotiations, routinely announce a State Advised Price (SAP) above the FRP; there is no constitutional bar on this, only an administrative/market tension with mill viability.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Sugarcane price deadlock nears resolution after 10-hour discussion with Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar
questions.pyqLink: Tests FRP vs SAP distinction in agricultural price policy, similar to UPSC's recurring MSP/CACP-based questions

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding drought declaration and relief in India:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The criteria and procedure for declaring drought are laid down in the Drought Management Manual, 2016 issued by the Union Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
Under the State Disaster Response Fund, the Centre contributes a larger share of the corpus for general category states than the concerned state government.
The 2016 Manual permits a state to declare drought solely on the basis of rainfall deficiency, without reference to other impact indicators such as soil moisture or crop condition.
A state government requires prior validation by the National Disaster Management Authority before it can officially declare drought in any district.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the 2016 Manual (Ministry of Agriculture) lays down drought criteria, and SDRF follows a 75:25 Centre-State sharing pattern for general category states (90:10 for special category states), consistent with Gujarat drawing on SDRF for the four declared districts. Statement 3 is wrong — the Manual mandates a multi-indicator, multi-trigger approach (rainfall plus vegetation, soil moisture and crop yield indices), not rainfall alone. Statement 4 is wrong — drought declaration is a state government decision based on the Manual's criteria; it does not require NDMA validation.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Gujarat govt. declares Devbhoomi Dwarka, Kutch, Jamnagar and Porbandar as drought-affected
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional/financial architecture of drought management, a recurring Disaster Management theme in GS-III/Prelims

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of institutions/concepts related to plant genetic resources and crop science:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources
Nodal institute under ICAR for collection and conservation of plant genetic resources in India
Svalbard Global Seed Vault
A backup seed storage facility located in Norway
Vavilov Centres of Origin
Geographic regions identified as possessing maximum genetic diversity of domesticated crop species
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology
Nodal body under the Department of Agriculture Research and Education for crop genome sequencing
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. Pair 4 is incorrect — CCMB functions under the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (Ministry of Science and Technology), not under the Department of Agriculture Research and Education; crop genomic studies like the Kashmir rice research are typically led by agricultural universities/ICAR institutes, not CCMB.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: In Kashmir's traditional rice, clues to a journey from East Asia
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional custodianship of agro-biodiversity, linked to the genetic-diversity findings in Kashmir's traditional rice study

questions.stem: Consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Sabarimala Ayyappa Temple is administered by the Travancore Devaswom Board, a statutory body.
In its 2018 verdict, the Supreme Court held that excluding women of menstruating age from the Sabarimala temple violated Articles 14, 15 and 17 of the Constitution.
The 'Sreekovil' of a Hindu temple refers to the outermost boundary wall enclosing the temple complex.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the Travancore Devaswom Board, constituted under the Travancore-Cochin Hindu Religious Institutions Act, 1950, administers Sabarimala, and the 2018 Indian Young Lawyers Association judgment struck down the exclusion as violating Articles 14, 15 and 17. Statement 3 is wrong — the Sreekovil is the sanctum sanctorum (innermost shrine housing the deity), not the outer boundary wall, which is why its gold cladding theft is significant.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Sabarimala gold theft case: Kerala HC directs SIT to expedite prosecution sanction
questions.pyqLink: Tests temple administration and architecture terminology alongside the landmark Sabarimala judgment, both recurring Culture/Polity PYQ themes

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Cyclones in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea are named from a list formulated under the WMO/ESCAP Panel on Tropical Cyclones, with the Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre at New Delhi as the designated naming authority.
The Bay of Bengal experiences a higher frequency of tropical cyclones than the Arabian Sea, mainly due to higher sea surface temperatures and lower vertical wind shear.
As per the India Meteorological Department's classification, a 'Very Severe Cyclonic Storm' is one with maximum sustained surface winds of 89-117 km/h.
Tropical cyclones in the Northern Hemisphere move from west to east throughout their life cycle due to the uniform effect of the Coriolis force.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct and standard syllabus facts about North Indian Ocean cyclogenesis and naming conventions, relevant as Cyclone 'Arnab' approaches the Andhra coast. Statement 3 is wrong — 89-117 km/h corresponds to a 'Severe Cyclonic Storm'; a 'Very Severe Cyclonic Storm' (the category assigned to Arnab) has sustained winds of 118-165 km/h. Statement 4 is wrong — cyclones typically move westward initially under trade winds and then recurve poleward/eastward under mid-latitude westerlies; motion is not uniformly west-to-east.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Cyclone 'Arnab' LIVE updates | 'Arnab' hurtling towards Andhra; Kakinada in the grip of fear
questions.pyqLink: Tests cyclone classification and steering mechanisms, a recurring Physical Geography PYQ area (e.g., UPSC questions on cyclone formation conditions)

questions.stem: With reference to the 'price cap' imposed by G7 countries and allies on Russian seaborne crude oil exports, which one of the following best describes this mechanism?
options: It imposes additional import tariffs on Russian crude entering G7 territory, raising its landed cost for domestic refiners
It prohibits Western shipping, insurance and financial services from being used to transport Russian oil sold above a specified price, without directly banning its purchase by third countries
It is a WTO-administered mechanism that caps the annual volume of crude oil Russia may export to non-G7 countries
It is a blanket European Union embargo banning all imports of Russian crude oil irrespective of price
questions.explanation: The G7/EU price cap (effective since December 2022) denies Western maritime services — shipping, insurance, financing — to any Russian crude cargo sold above the capped price, leveraging the West's dominance in tanker insurance rather than imposing a direct import ban; this has let third countries like India keep buying, with the narrowing discount reported by BPCL reflecting reduced sanctions-driven price leverage and higher freight costs via a 'shadow fleet'. It is not a tariff, a WTO volume quota, or a blanket EU embargo (the EU's separate import ban is distinct from the price cap mechanism).
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: BPCL shifts crude sourcing towards Middle East as Russian oil loses price edge
questions.pyqLink: Tests the mechanics of Western sanctions tools on Russian energy exports, relevant to India's energy diplomacy and import diversification

questions.stem: With reference to Special Leave Petitions (SLPs) under Article 136 of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Article 136 empowers the Supreme Court to grant special leave to appeal from any judgment, decree, determination, sentence or order passed by any court or tribunal in India, except those of courts martial.
The Supreme Court is constitutionally obligated to admit every Special Leave Petition filed before it.
A Special Leave Petition can be filed against a judgment or order of any High Court in the country, in both civil and criminal matters.
questions.explanation: Article 136 uses discretionary language ('may, in its discretion, grant special leave'), so the Court has a choice to hear or reject an SLP, not an obligation — Statement 2 is wrong. Statement 1 correctly describes the wide but not unlimited scope (court martial orders are excluded), and Statement 3 correctly notes SLPs cover both civil and criminal matters from any High Court.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Explained: Why the Supreme Court may be hearing too many Special Leave Petitions
questions.pyqLink: Tests the discretionary (not appeal-as-of-right) nature of Article 136, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on SC's original/appellate/advisory jurisdiction.

questions.stem: With reference to ethanol blending in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: E20 fuel refers to a blend containing 20% ethanol and 80% petrol, while E100 is a blend that is almost entirely ethanol.
Under India's existing regulatory framework, a vehicle certified only for E20 can be legally refuelled with E85 or E100 without any modification.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct — E20 is petrol with 20% ethanol and E100 is almost pure ethanol, as clarified in the recent Central Motor Vehicles Rules amendment. Statement 2 is incorrect: the rule change only expands the range of fuels that specially designed/certified flex-fuel vehicles may use — an E20-certified conventional petrol car cannot safely run on E85 or E100.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: In graphics: Centre’s new E100 fuel rule change and what it means for you
questions.pyqLink: Tests understanding of the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme and flex-fuel vehicle policy, an extension of past questions on biofuel categories.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding monsoon monitoring and drought in India. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) is the nodal agency responsible for monitoring and declaring the onset, withdrawal and all-India/regional deficit of the southwest monsoon.
El Niño refers to the warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean and is typically associated with weaker southwest monsoon rainfall over India.
A rainfall deficit of more than 60% compared to the Long Period Average is classified by the IMD as 'normal' monsoon rainfall for a region.
Declaration of drought in India is the sole prerogative of the Union Government under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, with no role for State Governments.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct — IMD monitors and reports monsoon rainfall data (as seen with its Ambalavayal station data in Wayanad), and El Niño years are historically correlated with below-normal Indian monsoon. Statement 3 is wrong, as IMD classifies a deficit beyond 60% as 'large deficient', not normal (normal range is within ±19% of LPA). Statement 4 is wrong because drought declaration is primarily done by State Governments using their own drought manuals, as illustrated by the Thirunelly panchayat urging the Kerala government, not the Centre, to declare drought.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: How community-based weather data is bolstering this Wayanad panchayat’s demand for drought-hit status
questions.pyqLink: Tests IMD's rainfall deficiency classification and the Centre-State division of disaster/drought declaration, a recurring static theme around monsoon-related current affairs.

questions.stem: With reference to snakebite management in India, consider the following statements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: All species of cobras found in India produce venom of identical composition, allowing a single antivenom to be equally effective against every cobra species.
In India, antivenom for snakebites is conventionally produced by immunising horses with venom and is typically polyvalent, designed to neutralise venom from more than one snake species.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct — India's conventional antivenom is raised in horses and is polyvalent, targeting the 'Big Four' venomous snakes. Statement 1 is false: the article explicitly notes that different cobra species, and even cobras of the same species from different locations, have differing venom composition, which is precisely the challenge the new nanobody-based antivenom seeks to address.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Different cobras have distinct venoms. How a new antivenom could treat them all
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of India's 'Big Four' venomous snakes and conventional polyvalent antivenom production, building on past questions on neurotoxic/hemotoxic venom and public health.

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of ocean-atmosphere phenomena and their descriptions. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
pairs: El Niño
Warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean
La Niña
Anomalous cooling of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean
Positive Indian Ocean Dipole
Warming of sea surface temperatures in the western Indian Ocean relative to the eastern Indian Ocean
Walker Circulation
A permanent atmospheric circulation cell over the Atlantic Ocean that drives the West African monsoon
questions.explanation: El Niño, La Niña and the positive Indian Ocean Dipole are correctly described — all three are genuine sea-surface-temperature anomaly patterns linked to Indian monsoon variability, relevant to the El Niño-linked rainfall deficit reported in Wayanad. The Walker Circulation pair is wrong: it is an equatorial atmospheric circulation over the Pacific Ocean (linked to ENSO), not a permanent Atlantic Ocean feature driving the African monsoon.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: How community-based weather data is bolstering this Wayanad panchayat’s demand for drought-hit status
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static geography of ENSO, IOD and Walker Circulation, concepts UPSC has repeatedly tied to monsoon-performance current affairs.

questions.stem: With reference to the 'Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage' (FRLD), recently in news over its first payout to Nepal, which one of the following best describes it?
options: A fund established under the World Bank's International Development Association exclusively to provide concessional loans for post-disaster reconstruction in least developed countries
A multilateral fund administered by the IMF to help member countries stabilise their balance of payments following climate-induced natural disasters
An international financing instrument operationalised under the UNFCCC process to provide financial assistance to developing countries particularly vulnerable to the adverse effects of climate change
A bilateral grant mechanism set up by G7 countries to finance renewable energy infrastructure in Africa and South Asia
questions.explanation: The FRLD was created in 2022 under the UNFCCC process to address the long-pending demand of developing and climate-vulnerable countries for assistance to cope with loss and damage from climate change, and its board made the first allocation to Nepal. It is not a World Bank IDA loan instrument, an IMF balance-of-payments facility, or a G7 bilateral mechanism, making the other options near-miss distractors.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Where Nepal’s $20 million flood relief money is coming from: the loss and damage fund’s first payout
questions.pyqLink: Tests the institutional architecture of UNFCCC climate finance mechanisms (Green Climate Fund, Adaptation Fund, FRLD), a frequently tested distinction in recent papers.
